2. Main ladder: sizing and construction

Step 1 — start a ladder

When flat, unpaused, out of cooldown and all applicable gates permit it, buy approximately $800 of HYPE. No SFP, support bounce or other positive setup is required. This is primarily a gated, repeatedly operating long ladder.

Step 2 — add exposure

Check roughly every 10 seconds. Another market buy becomes eligible when:

  • 30 minutes have elapsed since the last add; OR
  • the current price is at least 0.3% below the last surviving rung's fill.

Both routes still have to pass the entry gates. The price-drop route bypasses the waiting interval, not the trend/latch/cooldown/ownership checks.

These are market orders, not resting limit buys at each drop level. The price trigger normally uses the live bid; the actual buy fill can differ. Timer adds can occur above the previous entry: they do not require a pullback.

When there are already at least five rungs, the roughly 6h move from the rolling 5m context being ≤−0.5% doubles the timer to 60 minutes. The 0.3% price-drop route remains available.

Step 3 — size the next rung

next notional = $800 × 1.35^(number of currently open rungs). The base does not automatically compound upward with wallet profits. Live margin checks use refreshed wallet equity. initialCapital: 1000 in the JSON is a synthetic fallback, not the current ladder-account balance.

3. Main ladder: what blocks new exposure

These generally block first entries and/or adds; they do not themselves close existing positions. Exit rules are listed separately below.

GateExact condition / effect
HYPE trend breakLatest completed 4h close < EMA200 AND EMA50 is falling versus the previous completed 4h bar. Blocks first rung and adds. Below EMA200 alone is not enough.
BTC risk-offLatest completed BTC 1h close-to-close return <−3%. Blocks entries/adds for 120 minutes.
Damaged-regime latchCompleted HYPE 4h close ≤4% below EMA200, together with healthy HL taker 15m buy/sell ratio ≤0.85 OR 1h ratio ≤0.90. Remains blocked until two consecutive completed 4h closes are above −1% EMA200 distance.
Ladder-local killOldest surviving rung ≥12h and average-entry gross price PnL ≤−3%. Stops adding; does not flatten. It uses current age/current loss, not twelve continuous underwater hours.
Overextended first entryOnly while flat: HYPE 12h close-to-close move ≥2.55% AND 4h CRSI ≤56.9 AND 1h RSI ≥59.4. All three required.
Daily regime breakerFive consecutive lower daily closes block entries/adds; two consecutive non-lower daily closes release it. This is close-to-close, not candle-body colour. Despite its flatActive name it is an entry block, not an automatic close.
Forced-exit cooldownNo fresh exposure before the stored cooldown expires. See section 5.
Operational permissionManual pause, transaction/recovery conflicts, stale price feed, unavailable required finalized candles, incomplete continuous 48h Agg10 minute context, add-retry backoff, insufficient margin or unresolved maker-order handoff prevent adds.

Latch details: HL evidence uses a maximum 90s age, at least 14 samples for the 15m window and 55 for the 1h window. In normal operation, unavailable HL evidence does not invent a fresh trigger. An already-active latch persists through missing data and restart. First-time initialization while already below the −4% structure threshold can conservatively bootstrap the latch without HL confirmation. Releasing the latch does not override any other gate. The context gates also require healthy 14-day 5m coverage for the first-entry indicator calculation, and healthy 6h 5m coverage for the deep-add throttle.

4. Main ladder: take profit and S/R partials

Ordinary / stale batch TP

  • Target is based on the quantity-weighted average entry of all surviving rungs.
  • Normal target: +1.4%.
  • Under Aggressive10, the old 4h soft-stale reduction is deferred until the oldest surviving rung is 10h old. At/after that age, when current gross average-entry PnL is below +0.5%, the target becomes +0.5%.
  • This is a TP target adjustment, not a forced sale at 10h. The underlying soft-stale condition still applies; age alone is not an unconditional close.
  • Adding or partially closing inventory recalculates the average and TP.

Maker TP is enabled: one reduce-only PostOnly sell limit, rounded up to the exchange tick. Fee assumptions are 0.02% maker / 0.055% taker; actual fills determine realized fees. At a qualifying TP touch, the maker gets a 2s grace; an unfilled remainder goes through cancellation, reconciliation and market fallback. Unknown cancellation/order status blocks conflicting mutations rather than blindly sending another close.

The native TP stays during initial handoff, then is cleared only after the maker order is confirmed. It can be restored for safe handoff/fallback. This is not two independent full-size TP orders intentionally racing at the same trigger. Forced exits do not wait indefinitely for a maker fill.

Resistance partial exit — active

All are required:

  1. At least six rungs open.
  2. Healthy S/R context and confirmed resistance within 0.3% above price.
  3. Whole-ladder gross PnL ≥+0.25%.
  4. The proposed close basket is profitable after estimated entry and exit fees.
  5. The pulse is deteriorating, as defined below.
  6. The previous S/R partial-action 60-minute cooldown has expired.

Action: rank rungs by current dollar PnL, close the highest-PnL rungs with a market reduction and keep the three lowest-PnL rungs. This is not a fixed percentage trim and not necessarily keeping three particular rung numbers. The 60-minute cooldown limits further S/R partials; it is not a blanket add pause. Surviving positions retain their original entry times, and ordinary adds can rebuild the ladder if their gates permit.

Live S/R map: 30-minute pivots, four bars left/right for confirmation, 14-day memory, 0.45% clustering, at least two touches. The researched historical 4h/1d maps are not the production map for these partials.

Pulse deterioration is any one of:

  • Average available 4h HYPE OI change across Bybit/Binance/HL ≤−0.25%.
  • Binance HYPE 4h taker buy/sell-volume ratio ≤0.98.
  • BTC 4h move ≤−0.25%.
  • Negative funding on any of those HYPE venues AND either OI average ≤0% or Binance 4h taker ratio ≤1.05.

This partial's pulse gate is not the latch's HL 15m/1h rule.

5. Main ladder: full exits and cooldowns

All price-PnL percentages below are unleveraged price moves from weighted average entry, before fees/funding—not exchange margin ROE or account drawdown.

Full exitConditions
Emergency killAverage-entry gross PnL ≤−14%. No minimum age or hostile-trend requirement.
Funding-spike exit≥8 rungs and reported Bybit funding rate ≥0.00012 = 0.012%. No profit requirement.
Hard flattenOldest surviving rung ≥21h AND gross PnL ≤−2% AND hostile 4h trend (the EMA gate above). All three required.
Agg10 two-day-high exitOldest surviving rung ≥4h and the completed 1m close is within 1% below the rolling 48h high. No profit floor and no hostile-trend requirement. Full close, not a partial.
Weak-week time stop — Sep 25 additionAgg10 ladder age ≥40h AND completed-minute gross PnL ≤0% AND price ≤the exact minute close seven days earlier. No EMA/trend requirement.
Manual flattenOperator's explicit full-close signal; also pauses new ladder entries.

Important distinctions:

  • 21h alone does not force a close. A recovering/non-hostile ladder can outlive it.
  • 40h alone does not force a close either. A positive seven-day return, or a profitable ladder at the decision close, prevents this particular exit.
  • The 48h-high rule does not prevent the initial buy near a high. It closes an eligible existing ladder from age 4h; it is not a general high-proximity entry block.
  • The proposed 12h/−5% emergency branch is not implemented in this configuration.
  • The account-wide drawdown kill is disabled (maxDrawdownPct: 0). The −14% ladder emergency rule remains active and is a different control.

The closed-minute high and weak-week rules require healthy 48h minute context and a decision within the first 30 seconds after the minute closes. The weak-week rule additionally needs the exact seven-day reference candle; missing data does not authorize its close. Independent exits remain available.

Main-loop priority among enabled forced rules is emergency → funding spike → hard flatten → S/R partial → Agg10 high → weak-week stop. Ordinary maker/native/ WebSocket TP can complete independently; ownership/reconciliation resolves races. Pause blocks entries, not position management. Bot-side exits need the process, usable inputs and exchange access; the configured loss threshold is not a guaranteed fill.

After forced rule exits, the normal cooldown ends at:

(floor(exitTime / 4h) + 2) × 4h — roughly 4–8 hours, aligned to UTC 4h boundaries. For the new high/time-stop transaction paths, the completed execution anchors it; older forced branches use their loop decision clock. Example: exit at 13:10 UTC means next eligibility at 20:00 UTC. Ordinary Agg10 TPs have no hot-RSI cooldown.

At a full untouched $59,757 ladder, a −14% average-entry price loss is roughly −$8,366 before fees/funding/slippage. It is not a 14% loss limit on the account.

7. SF08 / LAWBSTER: step-by-step setup

Step 1 — identify a confirmed 4h range

  • Use completed HYPE 4h candles and strict pivots with two candles on each side. A pivot is not usable until its right-side confirmation bars are available.
  • Range low must be at least 24h old at the sweep.
  • Choose the highest qualifying later confirmed pivot high, known before the sweep, at least 2% above the low. This policy still requires high-after-low.
  • The range high must not already have been exceeded after its formation.

Step 2 — first sweep and closed reclaim

  • First eligible sweep trades at least 0.1% below the known range low.
  • Sweep must occur within the policy's 30-day eligibility window after low publication.
  • A completed 4h candle must then close back above that low, on the sweep bar or within the 24h reclaim window. No entry on the wick alone.
  • The range high must remain untouched through the reclaim, and above its close.
  • Gapped or late source context cannot be treated as a timely confirmed setup.
  • No RSI, CRSI, BTC, HL, POC, FVG, three-tap or additional structure-break filter is required. No extra confirmed higher-low/retest entry is required either.

Step 3 — fix the bracket, then buy once

Let C be the reclaim close and E the lowest price from sweep through reclaim:

Original structural stop S0 = E × 0.999
Original risk R             = C − S0
Take profit                 = C + 2 × R
Actual padded stop          = S0 × 0.95

Original risk must be 0.2%–5% of C. The extra stop padding is applied afterward. The TP remains the original absolute 2R price: it is not recalculated against the widened stop and is not necessarily the range high.

“5% SL” is shorthand for 5% below the structural stop, not below entry. At the reference close, the allowed original-risk band implies approximately 5.19%–9.75% distance to the padded stop. Actual fill and tick rounding change the exact distance. Example: reference $100, original stop $98 → TP $104, padded stop $93.10.

After the 4h close there is a 60s availability lag, then a 60s entry window. For example, a 12:00 UTC close can schedule an entry at 12:01, expiring at 12:02. Buy approximately $10,000 notional at market, quantity rounded down. The actual fill does not move the absolute TP or SL. TP rounds up to the price tick; SL rounds down. There is one position at a time and no averaging.

Step 4 — entry permission checks

  • VPS owner enabled, entries armed, lawbster-sfp-pause absent.
  • Correct pinned LAWBSTER identity, distinct from the ladder account; hedge mode, dedicated cross margin and 3× leverage as configured.
  • No pending transaction, recovery, unowned HYPE position or existing HYPE order.
  • Healthy timely signal, still inside its entry window; fresh valid bid/ask inside the fixed bracket; valid exchange quantity/tick/minimum notional.
  • Available margin at least notional / leverage + 0.2% of notional (about $3,353.33 for $10k/3×), plus the separate collateral check: equity must cover estimated loss to the SL plus 5% of notional reserve.

Signals encountered while paused, occupied or expired are consumed—not queued for a later buy. Restart does not replay a historical backlog. The same-minute exit guard prevents recycling an already-used decision minute.

These are account/execution safeguards, not the main ladder's market gates. The ladder can be trend-blocked or on cooldown while SFP remains eligible.

Step 5 — exits and protection

  • Native full-position market TP/SL, triggered by Bybit LastPrice.
  • 24h timeout from the scheduled signal action, not a new 24h clock on a late fill. Remaining inventory is market-closed even if the original structure still holds.
  • No partial TP, maker TP, trailing stop, breakeven move, scaling or 48h/72h timeout extension is live. SF09 remains research.
  • Three failed protection-confirmation polls request a fail-closed market exit. A missing/invalid liquidation estimate, or one not at least 0.5% below the SL, also requests exit. Those checks are conservative safeguards, not a guarantee against liquidation or slippage.
  • Pause/disarm affects new entries only; existing protection, reconciliation and timeout management continue, including when candle scanning is unavailable.
  • Realized trade accounting uses execution fees and is before funding.

The SFP owner polls about every 5 seconds. Its equity is separate; the accepted starting allocation was $5,269.72, not a claim about today's balance.

8. Alerts, controls and source pointers

SF08 has ordinary trade/close notifications and watchdog health coverage. Its approach warning is observational: in the final 10 minutes of a 4h candle, a valid known range + sweep + provisional reclaim can notify an armed, flat owner. At most one warning per setup and one setup per 4h close. A warning does not guarantee a final signal or order. The synced health includes a sent approach alert.

Requested sizes are not compounded. The configuration's initial equity is a reference figure; admission uses current verified USDT cash and owned inventory, not that hardcoded starting figure. Historical $19k results and their limits remain in the builder handoff.

Execution and ownership

  • One serial writer holds both HYPE side leases. Bybit aggregates each side; the durable lot ledger, not Bybit's blended entry, owns each strategy's cost, quantity, closes and receipts.
  • Main has one quantity-owned maker TP. A definitively failed PostOnly order can fall back to a quantity-owned conditional TP; no full-side TP is allowed. Maker-touch cancel/fill races settle before a residual market close.
  • SF08/PA07 attach Partial TP/SL to their entry. Parent-linked children must be reconciled before cancelling protection, closing a residual or releasing a slot.
  • Unknown submissions are never automatically resubmitted. Confirmed zero-fill main entry rejection starts a nonblocking five-minute retry backoff.
  • Real execution fees feed the ledger. Signed venue funding is separately attributed from executions; ambiguous settlements stay explicitly unallocated. The automatic funding reader overlaps seven days and is not a lifetime-backfill guarantee.
  • Old owner startup is refused while takeover is enabled; the portfolio also checks PM2 and the legacy pause files before writes. Do not run old deployed binaries beside it: those do not contain the new startup guard.
  • The cached worker supplies causal setup signals and main RSI/CRSI. Main RSI/CRSI preserve the parent's forming-HTF-from-known-minutes convention; auxiliary signals use their frozen closed-bar convention. Missing inputs block dependent entries; timed exits remain serviced.

Controls and alerts

portfolio-pause blocks entries, not exits. A persistent portfolio-flatten requests all portfolio owners drained, including late entry receipts, and leaves entries paused. portfolio-regime-arm resets only the daily regime-breaker memory, not the damaged-regime latch. Legacy Discord commands still address legacy signal files; use the portfolio runbook's controls until explicitly migrated. No dynamic rung override is supported.

Startup and filled-order notifications reuse Discord. The existing watchdog monitors the new owner when takeover is explicitly enabled, suppresses retired main/SFP/maker-shadow heartbeats, and retains collector monitoring. It reports missing heartbeat, sustained degradation, recovery and unconfirmed transactions. A paused/observing owner can be healthy without permission to trade.

Evidence and remaining release boundary

Offline checks reproduce 420 archived setup decisions, 61 MACD signals, 803 receipts and 48,156 capital formula comparisons. The cached feed matches 122,146 indicator/MACD feature comparisons; 104 main RSI/CRSI comparisons around a 4h boundary match the saved parent. This is component parity, not proof that a coupled live execution replay reproduces the full funded ladder portfolio.

The separate tiny short probe returned metadata_and_cleanup_passed, two children and observed_and_flat. That proves the reported metadata/cancellation/cleanup path, not native trigger races, production-size fills or liquidation safety. Preserve both probe reports; do not repeat them.

Documentation maintenance

This Markdown is the single maintained prose source; the browser edition is generated, self-contained HTML. The original date in the source filename is retained so existing links remain valid. Update the as-of and evidence statements when the rules or deployment status change, rather than making another copy.

Before committing/pushing live strategy changes, update the relevant sections and strategy runbook, then run:

node scripts/build-live-strategy-overview.cjs
node scripts/build-live-strategy-overview.cjs --test
node scripts/build-live-strategy-overview.cjs --check

Commit the source and generated HTML with the behavior/config change. The check compares the rendered guide and fingerprints relevant repository config/policy files. It reads no credentials or live account state.
